summary: Enrolling a passport photo failed with 'no face found in the image - use a clear, front-facing photo'. The photo was fine; the message was blaming it for a property of the DETECTOR'S INPUT. YuNet is anchor-based: it finds faces within a band of sizes RELATIVE to its input frame. A live camera frame - about 640px wide with a small distant face - sits comfortably inside that band, which is why recognition worked on cameras while the upload button refused the very photos people reach for. An uploaded photo is outside the band at BOTH ends. Measured against the shipped model on a plain-background portrait, at native size: 640x480 with the head at 35% of the height finds the face; 413x531 (a 35x45mm passport photo at 300dpi) with the head at 75% finds NOTHING; 1200x1600 at 60% finds nothing; 2448x3264 at 85% finds nothing. Four of five ordinary framings were refused, and every instruction the message gave ('use a clear, front-facing photo') sent the operator to look for a better photo, which cannot help. THE FIX is an enrolment ladder in ai/face_model.py: DOWNSCALE to a longest side of 640 (a 3000px-wide photo puts the face above the anchor range) and PAD with a margin (a head filling the frame leaves no context, and padding makes the face relatively smaller), tried as pad fractions 0.0/0.35/0.75/1.5 each followed by the downscale, stopping at the first rung that finds a face. The padding is a CONSTANT fill of the median edge colour rather than BORDER_REPLICATE: replicating the edge of a photo whose subject touches the border smears a face into the new margin, and a smeared half-face reported as a second face would trade 'no face found' for 'more than one face in the image'. Detection runs on the transformed copy and the rows are mapped BACK to original coordinates - using the per-axis scale actually applied after integer rounding, not the requested one, or every landmark lands slightly off - so alignCrop and the faceprint are computed at full resolution rather than from a 640px thumbnail. THE LADDER IS OFF FOR THE LIVE STAGE on purpose: live frames are already in the comfortable band, and an empty frame (the common case, many times a second) would otherwise cost four detections instead of one. Verified through the real path: faces_worker.py finds one face in a passport photo and in a 2448x3264 file, and both enrol over HTTP with quality 0.86/0.88. New bench tools/fleetbench/bench_face_enrol_framing.py asserts five framings each yield EXACTLY one face (the Go side refuses anything else) AND that each box lands on the subject - a mis-mapped box would still report one face and then embed the wrong pixels, which is a bad enrolment that poisons every future match instead of an error somebody can see. It draws its subject, so no photograph of a real person is committed. ErrNoFace now asks for 'the whole head visible', which after this fix is the one framing still refused and the only advice that helps.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no API, schema or config change. Live recognition is byte-identical - the ladder is a new opt-in argument (thorough=True) that only faces_worker.py passes. Faceprints enrolled before this remain valid and comparable: the ladder changes which photos are ACCEPTED, not how a face is aligned or embedded once found. Existing installs get the fix on the next enrolment with no restart - faces_worker.py is a one-shot process started per photo. Photos that were already accepted are unaffected (the first rung is the old behaviour plus a downscale that only applies above 640px). The refusal message text changed; the manual's People page gains a framing bullet in all four languages.
